subject: codex
title: execpolicy: standalone DSL crate for command-prefix and network allow/deny rules
one_why: Declarative policy evaluated before approval prompts; nuance vs generic permission-policy: the rules are a parsed DSL with its own parser and check tool, not config booleans.

subject: codex
title: OS-native sandbox on all three platforms with denial/violation tests
one_why: Enforcement is kernel-level and per-platform, with tests that assert denials actually fire - most harnesses only have one platform or advisory checks.

subject: codex
title: Three compaction tiers: summarization, remote-v2 with image budget, token-budget fresh-window
one_why: Falls back to a no-LLM fresh window when summarization is too expensive; all tiers share one lifecycle with pre/post-compact hooks (compact.rs:11-13).

subject: codex
title: Prompt-cache reuse gated on prompt_cache_key equality plus previous_response_id
one_why: Compaction/rollover decisions explicitly compare cache keys so a compaction never silently doubles the cache-miss bill.

subject: codex
title: End-to-end approval/suite tests against a scripted mock SSE responses server
one_why: 204 suite modules can assert full protocol event sequences with zero live API calls; the mock speaks the provider wire format, not an internal interface.

subject: codex
title: Guardian extension owns a reviewer pool that pre-warms review context for risky agent startups
one_why: A second-model review layer wired into core as an extension, with prewarm so review latency is off the critical path; no other subject has this.

subject: codex
title: Code-mode: agent drives tools by executing JS in a persistent v8 session over gRPC
one_why: Composable tool-calling inside a sandboxed interpreter session; field-defining if it sticks, hence unique not yet portable.

subject: codex
title: Sessions persisted as parseable rollout JSONL with materialize/fork/resume/archive commands
one_why: Journal is a stable decodable format (not DB state), enabling fork, --last resume, and third-party tooling over ~/.codex/sessions.

subject: codex
title: Network egress is sandboxed by default with a separate seatbelt network policy and approval flow
one_why: Outbound traffic is treated as a separate capability with its own ask flow; most harnesses leave egress wide open inside the sandbox.

subject: codex
title: No model evals or fuzz targets in-tree despite 440k LOC of tests
evidence: find over /data/samples/agents/codex for eval/fuzz dirs returns nothing
one_why: Verification anchor at 8 not 10: everything is deterministic protocol testing; behavior quality is presumably evaluated off-repo.
